messages:
Maria: quick heads-up — saw repeated tail latency spikes overnight in eu-west around 02:10. digging in and it looks like a single tenant flooding subslots and causing slab churn.
Adele: which tenant? any correlation with warm-pool activity?
Maria: tenant=carvana-prod. warm-pool looks normal but their short-burst jobs are evicting KV cache and we get a cascade.
Tom: can you paste the prometheus query you used?
Maria: sure, quick one i ran:
```
sum(rate(gpu_slab_allocs_total{region=\"eu-west\"}[5m])) by (tenant)
```
Maria: carvana is ~8x the next tenant during the spikes.
Josh: ugh. same tenant also had a big egress fanout last week. we cellared a soft-quota but maybe not enough.
Adele: proposal: add a "quiet reserve" slotting rule — keep N small dedicated slots per AZ for noisy-burst mitigation. when a tenant exceeds X allocs/min we route new bursts into quiet-reserve slots which are rate-limited at the proxy and have preseeded KV-cache.
Emily: what's the cost delta on keeping quiet-reserve warm? finance needs roughs.
Adele: ballpark: 2-3% fleet hours if we keep 1-2 slots per AZ warm. cheaper if we use fractional slices / preemptible for reserve and only warm the KV snapshot.
Tom: alternative is ventilation — periodic short drain of low-util tenants to create headroom before known traffic windows. think of it like a timed backfill window. cheaper but more complex.
Maria: i sketched a small config for a POC:
```yaml
quiet_reserve:
  per_az: 2
  preseed_kv: true
  rate_limit_qps: 50
ventilation:
  cadence: 1h
  drain_pct: 8
  exempt_tags: [sla-critical]
```
Josh: interesting. can we avoid SLA impact? exempt critical tenants obviously. and need a fast path fallback to dedicated if reserve is saturated.
Adele: yes — fallback chain: quiet-reserve -> dedicated-fractional -> hosted-fallback. routing policies updated. also need eviction backoff tweaks so we don't thrash.
Tom: operational concerns: scheduler metrics, rollback playbook, and telemetry to show we reduced tail P95. we should gate behind a canary in one AZ first.
Maria: +1 canary. i'll run the promql baseline and set alerts for slab-allocs-rate and kv-cache-miss spikes.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout to eu-west-a for quiet-reserve POC at 2026-03-22T09:00Z (eta 10m).
Emily: from cost perspective if this shaves 200ms tail and prevents a 2x cost spike for worst tenants, ROI looks good. need actual numbers from canary.
Josh: action items:
- Maria: baseline queries + alert rules (due: today)
- Adele: push POC config + scheduler hook (due: tomorrow)
- Tom: canary runbook + rollback steps (due: tomorrow)
- Emily: quick cost model with 1/3/6 month projection (due: Friday)
Maria: noted. will start alerts now. ping me if you want access to the dashboard.
Adele: i'll draft the routing policy PR and include a small sim.
Tom: i'll own the runbook and canary window.
Josh: thanks all. hope ventilation + quiet-reserve avoids the next noisy neighbor outage. :thumbsup:
Emily: please tag finance when you have estimated delta so we can approve reserve hours.
Maria: last note — if POC works, need to add a tenant-exempt list in console and a metric that shows "reserve hits" per tenant for billing/chargeback.
Adele: good call. will add telemetry hooks.
Maria: ok starting the data capture now.
